acceptance_criteria.given: A user enters a non-existent URL in the browser
acceptance_criteria.then: The user sees the custom error message and the 'Return to Home' button instead of the framework default.

acceptance_criteria.given: The user is on the 404 page
acceptance_criteria.then: They are redirected to the site's homepage.
acceptance_criteria.when: They click the 'Return to Home' button

acceptance_criteria.given: The user is navigating via keyboard
acceptance_criteria.then: The focus moves predictably to the 'Return to Home' button and follows the header/footer structure.

acceptance_criteria.given: The user has dark mode enabled in their system or site settings
acceptance_criteria.then: The colors and contrast conform to the site's dark theme specification.

assumptions.assumption: The sandbox site uses a standard Next.js App Router or Pages Router pattern that allows for a custom not-found component.
The existing theme provider handles CSS variable switching for light/dark modes automatically.

clarified_description: Replace the default Next.js framework 404 error page with a custom, branded 404 page for the Pixie sandbox site. The page will provide clear, plain-language feedback that the requested URL was not found and offer a single, primary call-to-action to return to the homepage. The page will be integrated into the existing site layout, including the global header and footer, and will support light/dark themes and accessibility standards.

constraints.detail: Must use existing Next.js routing patterns for 404 handling.
Ensure no sensitive system information or stack traces are leaked in the error message.

must: Display a custom message: 'The page you're looking for doesn't exist or has been moved. Check the URL or head back to the homepage.'
Provide a prominent 'Return to Home' button that links to the site root.
Integrate with the existing global site layout (Header and Footer).
Support both light and dark themes via the site's existing theme provider.
Meet WCAG accessibility standards (keyboard navigability and screen-reader compatibility).
outcome: Users encounter a branded, accessible error page instead of a broken framework default when they navigate to a non-existent URL.
rationale: A custom 404 page is a requirement for professional-looking sites. By including the header and footer, we provide context and prevent the user from feeling 'lost'. Keeping the navigation minimal (just a home button) reduces cognitive load during an error state.

risks.mitigation: Ensure the custom page only uses the approved static string and does not print the requested path or error objects directly to the DOM.
risks.title: Information Leakage

metrics: 404 error rate (to monitor if broken links are increasing elsewhere)

should: Include a subtle icon or graphic to visually reinforce the error state.

criteria: Message does not contain technical jargon
user_stories.so_that: I don't think the site is completely broken
user_stories.want: a clear explanation of why I can't see the page I requested

user_stories.so_that: I can quickly resume my task
user_stories.want: a single button to get back to the start

jobs_to_be_done: Navigate back to functional parts of the site
users.name: Site Visitor
pain_points: Confusion caused by generic framework error pages
Feeling stuck when a link is broken

children.text: The page you're looking for doesn't exist or has been moved. Check the URL or head back to the homepage.

wont: Include a sitemap or secondary navigation links.
Use a 'clean' layout that strips the header and footer.
